QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.prepared_by: Sarah Lee, Director of Quality Assurance
QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.approved_by: Dr. James Hartwell, VP Quality & Regulatory
QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.assessment_scope: Full QMS assessment against FDA QMSR (21 CFR 820 amended) incorporating ISO 13485:2016
QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.executive_summary: This gap analysis identifies areas where the existing QMS under 21 CFR 820 (QSR) requires modification to comply with the FDA Quality Management System Regulation (QMSR), effective February 2, 2026. The QMSR amends 21 CFR Part 820 to incorporate ISO 13485:2016 by reference, fundamentally changing the regulatory framework for medical device quality systems. A total of 23 gaps were identified requiring ISO 13485 clause mapping updates across 1,840 controlled documents.
QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.regulatory_background: On February 2, 2026, the FDA QMSR takes effect, amending 21 CFR Part 820 to incorporate ISO 13485:2016 by reference. The most significant change is the removal of the §820.180(c) exemption, which previously shielded management review records, quality audit reports, and supplier audit reports from FDA inspection. These records are now fully inspectable.

regulatory_changes.old_qsr_requirement: Management review, audit, and supplier audit records exempt from FDA inspection
regulatory_changes.new_qmsr_requirement: All records subject to FDA inspection per ISO 13485:2016 §4.2.5
New QSIT process aligned with ISO 13485:2016 structure

regulatory_changes.old_qsr_requirement: Risk analysis referenced but not ISO 14971 aligned
regulatory_changes.new_qmsr_requirement: ISO 13485:2016 requires risk-based approach throughout QMS per §7.1

QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.gap_analysis_summary: Analysis of the current QMS against ISO 13485:2016 requirements identified 23 gaps requiring remediation. Of these, 3 are classified as critical risk, 8 as high risk, and 12 as medium/low risk.

gap_items.gap_description: Document control procedure does not address §820.180(c) exemption removal — management review and audit records need updated retention and access controls
Record retention policy does not specify minimum device lifetime per ISO 13485:2016
Management review records not structured for FDA inspection readiness
Risk-based approach not fully integrated into production planning per ISO 13485:2016 §7.1
CAPA procedure terminology not harmonized with ISO 13485:2016 §8.5.2 and §8.5.3

QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.exemption_removal_impact: The removal of §820.180(c) represents the most operationally significant change. Management review records, internal quality audit reports, and supplier audit reports — previously exempt from FDA inspection — must now be maintained in an inspection-ready state.

inspectable_records.new_status: Subject to FDA inspection per ISO 13485:2016 §5.6
inspectable_records.compliance_action: Review and restructure management review outputs for inspection readiness

inspectable_records.new_status: Subject to FDA inspection per ISO 13485:2016 §8.2.4
inspectable_records.compliance_action: Ensure audit reports contain required objective evidence and corrective actions

inspectable_records.new_status: Subject to FDA inspection per ISO 13485:2016 §7.4.1
inspectable_records.compliance_action: Update supplier audit procedure and report template for FDA accessibility

QMSR_Gap_Risk_Analysis.recommendations: 1. Prioritize remediation of the 3 critical gaps related to §820.180(c) exemption removal before the QMSR effective date. 2. Complete ISO 13485 clause mapping for all 1,840 controlled documents. 3. Conduct training for all quality personnel on QMSR changes. 4. Update document templates to reference ISO 13485:2016 clause structure. 5. Establish a QMSR readiness review board to monitor remediation progress.

QMS_Document_Control_Report.document_control_summary: This report provides a comprehensive inventory of all controlled documents within the Quality Management System, with specific focus on documents impacted by the FDA QMSR transition effective February 2, 2026.
QMS_Document_Control_Report.revision_requirement_summary: The following documents have been identified as requiring revision to align with QMSR requirements, including updated ISO 13485:2016 clause references and removal of QSR-specific terminology.

documents_requiring_revision.title: Quality Manual
documents_requiring_revision.change_reason: Updated to align with FDA QMSR incorporating ISO 13485:2016; revised structure to match ISO clause numbering

documents_requiring_revision.title: Control of Documents Procedure
documents_requiring_revision.change_reason: Revised to address QMSR removal of §820.180(c) exemption

QMS_Document_Control_Report.compliance_notes: All 20 documents requiring QMSR revision have been updated and approved prior to the February 2, 2026 effective date. One Work Instruction (WI-SOL-045123) remains in DRAFT status pending final process engineer review. All document revisions include updated ISO 13485:2016 cross-references and removal of obsolete QSR-specific language.

CAPA_Completeness_Report.executive_summary: This report assesses the completeness of all Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPAs) within the 24-month assessment period in preparation for FDA QMSR compliance. Of 342 CAPAs assessed, 295 have been closed and 47 remain open. The CAPA population includes 198 corrective actions and 144 preventive actions. 14 closed CAPAs are missing required effectiveness verification — a critical finding given the QMSR's enhanced inspection requirements under ISO 13485:2016. 3 CAPAs are past due, and the average closure time is 62 days.

capa_records.description: Customer complaint - surface scratches on housing unit
Vendor complaint - raw material out of spec viscosity
Vendor complaint - contamination in chemical raw material

capa_tasks.task_description: Rework affected units - re-polish and re-coat housing surfaces
Implement automated surface inspection station after polishing step
Require supplier to complete infrastructure audit and replace corroded piping

CAPA_Completeness_Report.missing_verification_summary: The following 14 CAPAs have been closed but are missing required effectiveness verification per ISO 13485:2016 §8.5.2. This represents a compliance gap that must be addressed before FDA inspection under QMSR.

capas_missing_verification.description: Packaging seal integrity failure on sterile product line
Calibration drift on environmental monitoring sensors

CAPA_Completeness_Report.compliance_assessment: The CAPA system is largely compliant with ISO 13485:2016 §8.5.2 and §8.5.3 requirements. The primary compliance gap is the 14 CAPAs lacking effectiveness verification. Under the QMSR, FDA inspectors will have full access to CAPA records and may cite incomplete effectiveness verification as a nonconformity.
CAPA_Completeness_Report.recommendations: 1. Immediately initiate effectiveness verification for all 14 identified CAPAs. 2. Establish a 90-day maximum timeline for effectiveness verification after CAPA closure. 3. Update the CAPA procedure to include automated alerts for overdue effectiveness verifications. 4. Conduct a management review of CAPA metrics to identify systemic improvement opportunities.

Remediation_Plan.prepared_by: Sarah Lee, Director of Quality Assurance
Remediation_Plan.approved_by: Dr. James Hartwell, VP Quality & Regulatory
Remediation_Plan.executive_summary: This remediation plan addresses all identified gaps between the current QMS and FDA QMSR requirements. The plan encompasses document updates, process changes, training, and system modifications required to achieve full compliance by March 31, 2026.
Remediation_Plan.remediation_scope: The remediation plan covers all gaps identified in the QMSR Gap and Risk Analysis (RPT-GAP-2026-001), document control updates from the QMS Document Control Report (RPT-DOC-2026-001), and CAPA completeness findings from the CAPA Completeness Report (RPT-CAPA-2026-001).
Remediation_Plan.document_remediation_summary: The following document remediation tasks address the 23 controlled documents requiring updates for QMSR compliance, including ISO 13485:2016 clause mapping and removal of QSR-specific references.

document_tasks.change_description: Revise structure to ISO 13485:2016 clause numbering; add QMSR-specific requirements per 21 CFR 820.35
Address §820.180(c) exemption removal; update document retention requirements per ISO 13485:2016 §4.2.4
Update regulatory references from QSR to QMSR; add ISO 13485 clause cross-references

Remediation_Plan.capa_remediation_summary: The following tasks address CAPA-related findings, including the 14 CAPAs missing effectiveness verification and process improvements to the CAPA system.

Complete effectiveness verification for calibration drift CAPA
Implement automated 90-day effectiveness verification alerts in CAPA system

process_training_tasks.description: QMSR awareness training for all quality personnel (35 staff)

milestones.description: Complete QMSR gap and risk analysis across all QMS processes

Remediation_Plan.risk_assessment: The primary risk to the remediation timeline is the CAPA effectiveness verification backlog (14 CAPAs). If effectiveness verification reveals that corrective actions were not effective, additional CAPA cycles will be required, potentially extending the timeline beyond March 31, 2026. Mitigation: Prioritize the 3 critical CAPAs and allocate dedicated resources for verification activities.
